headline: Bitcoin is holding around $60,000 to $61,000 early Monday Bangkok time as forced selling cools after Saturday's crash, with a busy US holiday week of inflation data and a big options expiry ahead.

market.asOf: BTC and ETH from Binance price pages (timestamped 19:43 and 19:46 UTC Sun 22 Nov, 02:43 and 02:46 Bangkok). SOL from OKX's price page, timestamped 14:46 UTC, so it is several hours old. Prices move fast; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: 36 out of 100, "Fear", on the AltIndex crypto Fear & Greed Index (dated 22 Nov).

stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $60,000 as forced selling fades after the crash
stories.summary: After crashing to its lowest price in about two years on Saturday, bitcoin spent Sunday between roughly $58,000 and $61,000. The wave of forced selling has shrunk sharply, and most of what is still being force-closed now is bets on falling prices. Bitcoin is still about 25% lower than a month ago.
points: Bitcoin was about $60,728 on a CoinGecko snapshot, with a 24-hour range of $58,074 to $61,196, down 6.9% over 7 days and 25.4% over 30 days, per The Coin Republic.
Saturday's low was about $55,100 on Kraken and $55,711 on CoinGecko, per Cryptoticker.
CoinDesk put liquidations (forced closing of borrowed bets) at $2.40 billion over the crash, citing CoinGlass.
By Sunday evening the 24-hour liquidation total had fallen to about $134 million, $96 million of it bets on lower prices, per The Coin Republic citing CoinGlass.
The Coinbase Premium Index was about -0.21, meaning US buyers were paying slightly less than buyers elsewhere, per CryptoPotato.

stories.title: Saylor hints at another Strategy bitcoin buy as a big wallet pulls $1 billion off exchanges
stories.summary: Strategy, the company that holds 850,849 bitcoin, may announce another purchase: its chairman posted his usual hint on Sunday, but nothing is confirmed until the company files, normally on a Monday. Separately, on-chain trackers saw investment firm Abraxas Capital move about $1 billion of bitcoin off exchanges, which does not by itself prove a purchase.
points: Michael Saylor posted "The dots aren't done" on Sunday, his usual hint before a purchase, per crypto.news.
Strategy held 850,849 BTC bought at an average of $75,452 as of 15 Nov; last week it bought 485 BTC for about $33.4 million, per crypto.news.
Lookonchain says Abraxas Capital withdrew 17,597 BTC (about $1.04 billion) from Binance and Kraken; Arkham shows about 14,805 BTC of visible transfers, per The Coin Republic.
Strategy leaves the MSCI USA, World and ACWI indexes at the close of 30 Nov, per Yahoo Finance.

sources.label: crypto.news: Saylor hints at another bitcoin buy
The Coin Republic: Abraxas Capital withdrawals
Yahoo Finance: Strategy out of MSCI indexes

stories.title: Fund outflows and a crowded holiday week keep pressure on crypto
stories.summary: Money kept leaving US bitcoin and ether funds last week. This short Thanksgiving week brings US inflation data on Wednesday, with traders widely expecting the Fed to raise rates in December, and a large monthly bitcoin options expiry on Friday.
points: US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $1.25 billion over 16-20 Nov and ether ETFs $221.7 million, per crypto.news using Farside data.
BlackRock's IBIT lost $541.1 million on Thu 19 Nov, a record daily outflow, per crypto.news.
October PCE inflation and the second estimate of Q3 GDP are due Wed 25 Nov at 8:30am ET, per the BEA schedule; core PCE is expected around 3.2% a year against 3.1% before, per FXIFY.
Futures markets priced roughly a 95% chance of a quarter-point December hike, per FXIFY; Kiplinger put the odds above 97% on 20 Nov.
Bitcoin options covering 112,323 BTC, about $6.76 billion, expire on Deribit on Fri 27 Nov at 08:00 UTC, per Cryptoticker (Deribit data from 21 Nov).

sources.label: crypto.news: bitcoin and ether ETF outflows, 16-20 Nov

briefs.title: Chainflip hack losses rise to about $12 million; bounty deadline Monday
briefs.summary: The loss includes 122.86 BTC, 520.22 ETH, 3.25 million USDC and 758,141 USDT; Chainflip offers the attacker 10% if 90% comes back by 1:38pm ET (18:38 UTC) on Mon 23 Nov, and the FLIP token fell about 37%, per The Block.

briefs.title: Kalshi faces a Monday court hearing in New York
briefs.summary: A Manhattan state court hears New York Attorney General Letitia James's request for a restraining order on Mon 23 Nov at 11:30am ET; Kalshi says it would shut its exchange for every customer, everywhere, per The Block.

briefs.title: Kraken's bitcoin-Canadian dollar market briefly crashed to about US$16,900
briefs.summary: BTC/CAD traded at C$24,250 around 08:00 UTC on Saturday, about 71% below the US dollar price; Kraken says there was no breach and executed trades stand, per Cointelegraph.

briefs.title: Coinbase reportedly plans its own prediction markets
briefs.summary: Coinbase is reportedly aiming to launch in-house prediction markets in the US in the first half of 2027, per Bloomberg as reported by Bitcoin.com News; Coinbase declined to confirm.

briefs.title: TRUMP memecoin dinner draws far less interest
briefs.summary: Only 130 wallets holding a combined $8.6 million qualified for Sunday's dinner, and one holder got in with a $518 buy, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: BTCS warns its $54 million Aave loan could be liquidated
briefs.summary: The Nasdaq-listed ether holder told the SEC its loan could be liquidated if ether falls to about $1,450; its shares fell 28.1% on the week, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Solana drops its "beta" label
briefs.summary: Solana's mainnet moves to version 1.0 with nothing for users to do, and the Solana Foundation now holds a majority stake in price site CoinGecko, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: Bitcoin miners' earnings stay weak; Bitcoin Core fixes a bug
briefs.summary: Hashprice, miners' revenue per unit of computing power, fell to $26.16 per PH/s per day, and Bitcoin Core fixed a medium-severity bug that could stall nodes but not steal coins, per Yahoo Finance.

Manufacturing is expected at 54.5 (October: 54.9) and services at 55.6 (October: 56.1), per FXEmpire.

calendar.event: New York court hearing on Kalshi
calendar.note: Justice Melissa Crane hears the New York Attorney General's request for a restraining order; Kalshi says it would shut its exchange nationwide, per The Block.

calendar.event: New York Fed President John Williams speaks
calendar.note: Remarks on the economic outlook and monetary policy, followed by Q&A, per the New York Fed.
Expected at 92.1 after 91.7 in October, per FXEmpire.

calendar.event: Dell, HP Inc and Workday earnings
calendar.note: All three report after the US close on Tue 24 Nov, per FXEmpire.

calendar.event: US PCE inflation (Oct), Q3 GDP (second estimate), durable goods and jobless claims
calendar.note: Core PCE is expected around 3.2% a year (prior 3.1%), per FXIFY. Q3 GDP is expected at 3.5% after 3.4% before, durable goods at 0.5% after 1.9%, and weekly jobless claims at 201K after 203K, per FXEmpire. Times per the BEA schedule.
The Fed's survey of business conditions around the country, per the Fed. New home sales come out earlier the same day at 10:00am ET (22:00 Bangkok); 649K is expected after 676K, per FXEmpire.
US stock and bond markets are closed, and on Friday 27 Nov stocks close early at 1:00pm ET (01:00 Sat Bangkok), per Admiral Markets. Crypto trades all day, but thin trading can mean bigger swings.

calendar.event: Monthly bitcoin options expiry on Deribit
calendar.note: About $6.76 billion of bitcoin options (112,323 BTC) expire, with the "max pain" level at $73,000, per Cryptoticker using Deribit data from 21 Nov; CoinOtag put it at about $6.6 billion on 22 Nov.
Comes out before the Fed's 9 Dec decision, per the BLS schedule. November CPI is Thu 10 Dec, the day after the Fed decision, per the BLS.

calendar.event: Next Fed meeting and rate decision
calendar.note: Two-day meeting 8-9 Dec; the decision is at 2:00pm ET on Wed 9 Dec (02:00 Thu Bangkok), with a press conference at 2:30pm ET, per the Fed. Fed officials stop public comment on policy from Sat 28 Nov, per FXIFY. Futures priced roughly a 95% chance of a quarter-point hike, per FXIFY.
